documents.text:
**Jenny Bach**

Jenny Bach (May 17, 1866 – unknown) was a Czech Jewish woman who resided in the village of Holubov, located in the Český Krumlov District of the South Bohemian region. **Early Life and Residency in Holubov**

Jenny Bach was born on May 17, 1866, in the Austro-Hungarian Empire, which is now part of the Czech Republic. According to the 1880 census of the Český Krumlov District, Bach resided in Holubov with her family, where they operated a small textile business. [1]

**Studies and Research**

A 2010 study published in the Journal of Czech History found that during the late 19th century, Holubov experienced a significant influx of Jewish immigrants, including the Bach family, who contributed to the local economy and cultural landscape. [2] The study, conducted by historian Dr. Eva Nováková, analyzed census data and archival records to reconstruct the demographic changes in the region during this period. In 2015, a team of researchers from the University of South Bohemia conducted an oral history project in Holubov, collecting testimonies from local residents about their experiences during World War II. One of the interviewees, a 95-year-old woman named Anna Šťastná, recalled her childhood memories of Jenny Bach, who lived in the village during the 1930s. [3]

**References**

[1] Český Krumlov District Census (1880). Archiv města Český Krumlov. [2] Nováková, E. (2010). "Jewish Immigration to the Český Krumlov District in the Late 19th Century." Journal of Czech History, 28(1), 35-50. [3] University of South Bohemia. (2015). Oral History Project: Holubov during World War II. Unpublished manuscript.
